newsitem.title: USA: CBO puts U.S. FY97 budget deficit at $34 bln.
newsitem.headline: CBO puts U.S. FY97 budget deficit at $34 bln.

text.p: The Congressional Budget Office on Wednesday cut its projection for the U.S. budget deficit to $34 billion for fiscal 1997, down from a previous estimate of $67 billion.
Continuing strong growth in receipts and a slowdown in outlay growth were responsible for the drop, the CBO said.
It projected total receipts for the year at $1.578 trillion, up from its May estimate of $1.555 trillion, and outlays at $1.612 trillion, down from $1.622 trillion.
Fiscal 1997 runs from October 1, 1996, to September 30, 1997.
The deficit for fiscal 1997 would be down from $107 billion in fiscal 1997 and would be the lowest since 1974.
Earlier on Wednesday, President Bill Clinton said at a news conference that the White House saw the deficit for the year at $37 billion.
But a CBO analyst said there was no significant disagreement with the White House figure as both were estimates.

The CBO said it based its latest estimate on Treasury Department figures showing a monthly budget surplus of $54.5 billion for June. For the first nine months of the fiscal year, the deficit was $10.9 billion, compared with $74.0 billion for the same period of fiscal 1996, Treasury said.
CBO estimated the monthly deficit for July at $25.5 billion, compared with $26.9 billion in July, 1996.

Commenting on the latest CBO figures, Senate Budget Committee chairman Pete Domenici, R-New Mexico, said: "By holding the line on federal spending while creating an environment for growth and job creation we have been able to bring the deficit to its lowest level since 1974."
